subject: Hosted API volume discount mechanics — clarification on streaming rounding and billable-token language
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: sarah.cole@atlashealth.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API volume discount mechanics — clarification on streaming rounding and billable-token language

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I attached the proposal (Redwood_Proposal_v3.pdf) and a short FAQ on how we meter hosted usage. Two quick points you asked me to confirm for procurement:

1) How we define "Billable Token" and whether streaming mode uses a different rounding unit than standard completion calls.
2) How rounding/aggregation affects true-up and whether Atlas can cap rounding overhead for predictable billing.

Short answers up front: our default hosted metering counts billable tokens per request for non-streaming calls and aggregates streaming data into per-second accruals that are converted back into token-equivalents using a defined mapping; rounding is applied at the conversion step, by default to the nearest whole token, but enterprise contracts can specify per-call rounding or a monthly aggregation rule.

Before I put formal contract language together I wanted to surface two examples that procurement liked in other accounts and check what Atlas needs:
- Option A (per-call rounding): round up each request to nearest 1 token (simplest, deterministic per-call).
- Option B (streaming accrual then monthly aggregate): accumulate streaming bytes/sec for each session, convert to token-equivalents at the end of the month, then apply rounding once per session or once per account-month (reduces rounding overhead for high-freq, sub-token events).

Could you confirm whether Atlas prefers a deterministic per-call billing number, or monthly-aggregated billing with an explicit rounding cap (e.g., no more than 0.5% rounding overhead per month)? Also flag any auditability requirements (need for example calculations in the contract appendix, or a right to request a month of usage logs).

Copying Marcus (pricing lead) and Hannah (contracts) — they can propose the exact clause once we hear back.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the quick note and the proposal. A few clarifications from our side so your legal/pricing teams can draft precise language: please read the three asks below and respond with specific contract text and an example table of calculations.

1) Definition: We need a single canonical definition for "Billable Token" that applies across non-streaming and streaming modes. For example: "Billable Token: the unit of usage, derived from the model's tokenization, used to compute charges and discounts." Please indicate whether you tie this to a particular tokenizer version (we prefer language that remains stable as models change).

2) Rounding/aggregation behavior: We observed with another vendor that streaming responses produced many small increments that were rounded up per-chunk and doubled our token bill compared to post-hoc aggregation. Procurement asks for either (a) explicit per-month aggregation, with rounding applied once at the account-month level, or (b) per-session aggregation with a maximum rounding overhead cap (e.g., no more than 1% additional billable tokens per month attributable to rounding). Which option is standard for Redwood enterprise customers?

3) Auditability & true-up: We need a transparent true-up process. If Atlas believes rounding/aggregation materially changed invoiced usage vs. expected usage, we want the ability to request raw usage logs for the disputed month and a one-time adjustment if rounding overhead exceeds the contract cap. Please confirm Redwood's willingness to include a 45-day dispute window and sample raw logs sanitized for PII.

If you can send proposed contract snippets that map to these three items and an example monthly calc (example: a 10-hour streaming session with 3 concurrent streams => X raw events => Y tokens by per-call rounding vs. monthly aggregation) that would move us to legal review.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 30-min call if easier.

Best,
Sarah
Director of Product, Atlas Health
sarah.cole@atlashealth.com

Internal — forwarding Atlas questions. Notable asks: canonical Billable Token definition, option for monthly aggregation OR per-session aggregation with a rounding cap, auditability + 45-day dispute window and sample logs (sanitized).

My thoughts:
- Pricing: we usually offer monthly aggregation for enterprise accounts at or above the 1B token commit; per-session cap is an alternative when customers want streaming latency determinism. For Atlas (targeting 750M/mo initial commit) we should propose monthly aggregation with a 0.5% rounding overhead cap and a built-in true-up mechanism. That keeps their bills predictable and protects Redwood from extreme edge cases.
- Legal: we need to define the tokenizer tie-in carefully — prefer referencing "Billable Token as measured by Redwood's production tokenizer as of the invoice date" with a change-management paragraph (30-day notice before changing tokenizer or retroactive recalculation rule).

Can you draft two short clauses: one for Billable Token definition + tokenizer stability, and one for Rounding & Aggregation (including the cap and audit process)? Also, confirm whether adding a table of example calcs to an appendix (non-normative) is acceptable.

— Laura

Hi Sarah / Atlas procurement team —

Thanks for the clear asks. Per Marcus and Hannah's input, below is proposed contract language you can share with Atlas legal. I also attached a small CSV (billing-examples.csv) with three worked examples (per-call rounding vs monthly aggregation vs per-session aggregate) using numbers close to Atlas's expected workload.

Proposed (redlined) snippets — please treat these as starting text:

1) Definition — Billable Token
"Billable Token" means the unit of usage used to compute charges under this Agreement. For Hosted API calls, Billable Tokens are derived from Redwood's production tokenizer as of the invoice date. Redwood will provide, upon Customer's written request, a non-normative appendix with example mappings from request size to Billable Tokens for commonly used model families. Any change to Redwood's tokenizer or tokenization methodology that materially affects Billable Token counts will be communicated at least thirty (30) days in advance; such changes will not be applied retroactively to settled invoices.

2) Rounding and Aggregation
a) Non-Streaming Calls: Billable Tokens for a non-streaming request are the number of tokens produced by Redwood's production tokenizer for the request and response, rounded up to the nearest whole token per request.

b) Streaming Calls: For streaming responses, Redwood will accrue usage continuously and convert streaming accruals to Billable Tokens at the end of the invoice month. The conversion will use Redwood's documented mapping of bytes/sec to token-equivalents (documented in the non-normative appendix). Rounding will be applied once at the account-month level (i.e., after monthly aggregation) unless Customer elects per-session aggregation in writing prior to the effective month.

c) Rounding Overhead Cap: For customers on an enterprise commit, Redwood will ensure that rounding and aggregation behavior does not increase invoiced Billable Tokens by more than 0.5% in any invoice month compared to a hypothetical exact-token accounting (as measured by Redwood's production logs). If rounding overhead exceeds the cap for a given month, Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to the excess tokens multiplied by the applicable per-token rate for that month.

3) Auditability and True-up
Customer may dispute invoiced usage within forty-five (45) days of invoice issuance. During a dispute, Customer may request Redwood provide the pertinent usage logs for the disputed month (logs will be redacted for PII and production identifiers as mutually agreed). Redwood will investigate and, if the rounding/aggregation behavior materially impacted invoice totals beyond the Rounding Overhead Cap, Redwood will issue an appropriate credit within thirty (30) days of resolution.

Notes & appendix: we propose adding the billing-examples.csv to the contract appendix as an illustrative, non-normative attachment. The appendix will include three worked examples (sample streaming session, per-call completion, and mixed workload) and a short table showing impact on billing for the proposed 750M/mo commit and the proposed discount breakpoint (750M => 12% off list, 2B => 18% off list).

If this looks reasonable I can ask legal to put it into the next draft and we can get a short SOW/PO in to lock the initial commit pricing while legal finishes the redlines.

Would you like a 30-minute call Monday to walk through the CSV examples?

Thanks,
